newsitem.title: USA: IPO SPOTLIGHT - Simulation Sciences seen hot.
newsitem.headline: IPO SPOTLIGHT - Simulation Sciences seen hot.

text.p: Shares of Simulation Sciences Inc, a chemical-engineering software supplier, should make a solid debut on Friday, with the company representing what analysts called an untapped market with strong potential.
Bob Austrian, an enterprise software analyst at Montgomery Securities, said the simulation software market has "low penetration but a lot of potential."
"It's a big market with not a lot of solutions yet used in that market," he said. "It has untapped possibilites -- there are potential customers that aren't using these products yet."
Although Simulation's initial public offering could be overlooked amid the high number of IPOs due Friday, many analysts expect the stock to do well, particularly over time.

David Menlow, president of the IPO Financial Network, said the deal was on his "hot list," but initially "the stock may end up being softer." Almost 20 companies are tentatively on deck to go public Friday.
David Farina, a software analyst at William Blair & Co, would not comment on the IPO, though he said the demand for simulation products was strong.
Simulation Sciences is a provider of Windows-based simulation software to the processing industries, including petroleum, petrochemical and industrial chemicals.
Its products help to reduce capital investment costs, improve plant yields and enhance management decision-making, according to the company's prospectus.
Farina said the company's closest competitor is Aspen Technology Inc, a Cambridge, Mass.-based supplier of software for analysis, design and automation of process manufacturing plants.
Aspen stock has more than quadrupled since its IPO in October 1994. It went public at $13 a share and closed on Thursday at 60-3/4 on the Nasdaq.
"Aspen Technology was a yawn of a deal," when it first went public, Farina said, "but it's a good stock now."
As with Aspen Technology, Simulation Sciences would probably appeal to growth investors interested in technology, he said.
The offering of 3.6 million common shares is expected to be priced at between $8 and $10 a share, according to Alex Brown & Sons Inc, lead underwriter for the deal.
The Brea, California-based company is offering 2.7 million shares, while 900,000 are being offered by certain stockholders.
Simulation Sciences reported revenue of $21.8 million for the six months ended June 30, compared with revenue of $15.2 million for the first half of 1995.
It posted a profit of $1.4 million in 1995.
The company has filed to trade its stock on the Nasdaq National Market under the symbol "SMCI."
